Join Xurrent, where our AI-driven Operations Management platform powers the way modern enterprises manage and evolve their service delivery. We’re looking for curious, driven individuals who want to make a real impact and grow with a company leading the next wave of service and operations innovation.

Mission: As an Associate Account Executive, you'll play a key role in driving our growth by winning new business across the UK market. This is a full-cycle sales role for someone who enjoys opening doors, building relationships, and closing deals in a fast-paced B2B SaaS environment.

You'll own the entire sales process—from identifying and prospecting high-potential accounts through to discovery, solution positioning, negotiation, and close. Success in this role comes from building your own pipeline, consistently delivering new business, and partnering with prospects to solve meaningful business challenges. In addition to winning new logos, you'll identify opportunities to grow existing customer relationships where appropriate.

This is a hybrid role based in our London office, onsite presence is required Monday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Responsibilities:  

  • Own and execute a strategic territory and account plan to consistently drive new business growth.
  • Consistently achieve and exceed quarterly and annual sales targets.
  • Build, manage, and progress a high-quality sales pipeline through a combination of outbound prospecting, inbound opportunities, and partner-generated leads.
  • Manage the full sales cycle, maintaining accurate pipeline, forecasting, and opportunity data in CRM and other sales tools.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Customer Success, Sales Engineering, Product, and Support teams to deliver an exceptional buying experience and continuously improve the sales process.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with channel and technology partners to identify and accelerate new business opportunities.
  • Clearly articulate Xurrent's value proposition, business outcomes, and competitive differentiation to technical and executive-level stakeholders.
  • Stay informed on market trends, customer challenges, and the competitive landscape to effectively position Xurrent's solutions.
  • Represent Xurrent at industry events, customer meetings, and strategic conferences to build brand awareness, generate pipeline, and strengthen customer relationships.

Minimum Requirements 

  • 2+ years of experience as a Business Development Representative (BDR) or Sales Development Representative (SDR) in a B2B SaaS environment, with a proven track record of consistently achieving or exceeding quota.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to deliver compelling product demonstrations and engage technical and business stakeholders throughout the sales process.
  • Experience collaborating cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success teams.
  • Experience using a CRM platform (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar) to manage pipeline, maintain accurate opportunity data, and support forecasting.
  • Strong organizational skills, commercial acumen, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • A proactive and entrepreneurial approach, with a commitment to maintaining a disciplined and structured sales process.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in IT Service Management (ITSM), Enterprise Service Management (ESM), or a related enterprise SaaS market.
  • Experience progressing opportunities beyond initial discovery, including supporting product demonstrations, commercial discussions, or closing activities.
  • Experience selling to mid-market or enterprise organisations and engaging multiple stakeholders throughout the buying process.
  • A growth mindset with a strong desire to learn, develop, and progress into a successful Account Executive.

Compensation

  • Base: £40,000–£65,000, depending on experience
  • Commission: £40,000–£65,000
  • On-Target Earnings (OTE): £80,000–£130,000

closest.location: South San Francisco, California, United States
closest.text:
About Xaira Therapeutics

Xaira is an innovative biotech startup focused on leveraging AI to transform drug discovery and development. The company is leading the development of generative AI models to design protein and antibody therapeutics, enabling the creation of medicines against historically hard-to-drug molecular targets. It is also developing foundation models for biology and disease to enable better target elucidation and patient stratification. Collectively, these technologies aim to continually enable the identification of novel therapies and to improve success in drug development. Xaira is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, and London.

About the Role

We are seeking a Lab Automation Engineer Contractor to program, operate, and maintain liquid handling platforms and integrated workcells supporting protein production, analytical, and next-generation sequencing workflows.

This hands-on role is responsible for keeping laboratory automation systems running reliably. You will support daily operations, translate established protocols into automated methods, troubleshoot equipment and workflows, perform routine instrument maintenance, and coordinate service with manufacturers.

We are looking for a dependable, hands-on team member who takes ownership of laboratory automation operations. The ideal candidate combines practical liquid-handling experience with strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities

You will program, modify, test, and operate liquid handling methods. This includes preparing labware and reagents, monitoring automated runs, documenting deviations, and supporting recovery from workflow interruptions.

You will help keep laboratory instruments and integrated workcells operational through routine and preventive maintenance, calibration checks, light repairs, and structured troubleshooting. You will also coordinate service and repair with manufacturers when needed.

You will operate integrated automation systems, including liquid handlers, plate storage and transport systems, analytical instruments, and scheduling software. You will maintain SOPs, troubleshooting guides, maintenance records, and operating instructions.

You will also support sample tracking, run documentation, and data transfer to LIMS, ELN, and downstream systems, while training and supporting scientists and operators who use the automation equipment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Bioengineering, Biotechnology, Biology, Chemistry, or a related field, or equivalent relevant industry experience.
  • At least 1 year of industry experience working with automated liquid handling systems in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, or life sciences.
  • Demonstrated experience programming and troubleshooting automated liquid handlers.
  • Basic programming or scripting experience in Python, C#, or another language used for laboratory automation and instrument integration.
  • Experience maintaining or servicing laboratory instruments, including preventive maintenance, basic calibration, light repair, and coordination with equipment manufacturers.
  • Working knowledge of molecular biology and analytical laboratory techniques, including PCR, gel electrophoresis, plate-reader assays, or HPLC.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across laboratory hardware, software, labware, reagents, and operating procedures.
  • Ability to document technical issues, maintenance activities, and workflow deviations clearly and consistently.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and commitment to safe and reliable laboratory operations.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills across scientific, engineering, operational, and vendor teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Hamilton liquid handlers, including method development, liquid classes, deck configuration, error recovery, and routine maintenance.
  • Experience operating integrated automation workcells and orchestration platforms such as Cellario, Green Button Go, Momentum, or similar schedulers.
  • Familiarity with laboratory informatics systems such as LIMS and ELN, including sample tracking, metadata capture, result transfer, and workflow traceability.
  • Experience connecting laboratory instruments or automation systems through device drivers, APIs, middleware, serial or network communication, or IoT integration frameworks.
  • Experience supporting protein production, purification, analytical, or NGS workflows in a research or production environment.

About Xaira Therapeutics

Xaira is an innovative biotech startup focused on leveraging AI to transform drug discovery and development. The company is leading the development of generative AI models to design protein and antibody therapeutics, enabling the creation of medicines against historically hard-to-drug molecular targets. It is also developing foundation models for biology and disease to enable better target elucidation and patient stratification. Collectively, these technologies aim to continually enable the identification of novel therapies and to improve success in drug development. Xaira is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, and London.

About the Role

We are seeking a Lab Automation Engineer Contractor to program, operate, and maintain liquid handling platforms and integrated workcells supporting protein production, analytical, and next-generation sequencing workflows.

This hands-on role is responsible for keeping laboratory automation systems running reliably. You will support daily operations, translate established protocols into automated methods, troubleshoot equipment and workflows, perform routine instrument maintenance, and coordinate service with manufacturers.

We are looking for a dependable, hands-on team member who takes ownership of laboratory automation operations. The ideal candidate combines practical liquid-handling experience with strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities

You will program, modify, test, and operate liquid handling methods. This includes preparing labware and reagents, monitoring automated runs, documenting deviations, and supporting recovery from workflow interruptions.

You will help keep laboratory instruments and integrated workcells operational through routine and preventive maintenance, calibration checks, light repairs, and structured troubleshooting. You will also coordinate service and repair with manufacturers when needed.

You will operate integrated automation systems, including liquid handlers, plate storage and transport systems, analytical instruments, and scheduling software. You will maintain SOPs, troubleshooting guides, maintenance records, and operating instructions.

You will also support sample tracking, run documentation, and data transfer to LIMS, ELN, and downstream systems, while training and supporting scientists and operators who use the automation equipment.

  • Experience operating integrated automation workcells and orchestration platforms such as Cellario, Green Button Go, Momentum, or similar schedulers.

closest.title: AI Engineer
closest.text:
About us

At Xelix, we work with some of the world’s largest companies to automate and strengthen their financial controls. Our AI solutions redefine how Accounts Payable teams operate – moving from manual processes to automated, intelligent workflows.

Xelix is a fast-paced scale-up – things move fast and expectations are high. We raised our Series B with Insight Partners in June 2025 and are expanding aggressively. We have a team 150 talented people pulling together to achieve our goals. Everyone is trusted to take ownership, move fast and have a meaningful impact. We prioritise personal and professional growth, keep things fun, and love to celebrate a milestone together.

In this role you’ll grow, be challenged and help shape the future of Xelix. If you’re excited about building something special with us, we’d love to hear from you.

About the role

We are hiring an AI Engineer to join our growing AI Engineering team. You’ll design and build production AI systems — combining machine learning, large language models, and strong engineering — to solve real problems across documents, email, and financial data.

We focus on building systems that work reliably in production, not just prototypes. We use modern AI tools extensively in our workflow, enabling engineers to operate at a higher level — focusing on system design, product thinking, and solving complex problems.

What you'll be doing

  • AI Systems & Agents: design and build production AI systems — including agent-based workflows, tool use, and multi-step reasoning.

  • Model Development & Adaptation: develop and improve models across text, vision, and structured data, including fine-tuning and hybrid ML + LLM approaches.

  • LLM Platform Work: work with hosted and self-hosted models, contributing to decisions around model selection, performance, and cost.

  • Production Engineering: write clean, maintainable Python and contribute to scalable, observable systems.

  • Evaluation & Iteration: design evals, measure performance rigorously, and improve systems using real-world feedback.

  • AI-Assisted Development: use modern AI coding tools to move faster while maintaining high standards.

  • Collaboration: work closely with product and engineering teams to deliver high-impact features.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience: 2–5 years building and shipping ML or AI-powered systems into production.

  • Strong Engineering Skills: clean, testable Python; solid software design; experience working in production environments.

  • AI/ML Breadth: experience with either traditional ML (e.g. gradient boosting) and/or LLM systems (prompting, tool use, evals, agents).

  • Systems Thinking: ability to reason about trade-offs (accuracy, latency, cost, reliability) and design accordingly.

  • Data Skills: SQL, pandas, and experience working with messy real-world data.

  • AI-Native Workflow: comfortable using AI-assisted coding tools effectively.

  • Curiosity & Ownership: proactive in exploring new approaches and improving existing systems.

  • Collaboration: strong cross-functional working style.


What we offer in return

💰 Competitive salary of £65,000 to £75,000 depending on experience

🏝️ 27 days of annual leave (including 3 days Christmas closing) which increases up to 3 days based on tenure, with the option to roll over, buy or sell up to 3 days

🏡 Hybrid working with two days a week from our dog-friendly Hoxton office

💪 On-site gym and cycle to work scheme

🛍️ Employee discount at over 100 retailers

🏥 Comprehensive private medical & dental cover with Vitality

🍼 Enhanced parental leave pay

📚 Learning & development culture – £1,000 personal annual budget

🌍 We’re carbon-neutral and are working towards ambitious carbon reduction goals

🎯 Lots of team socials & activities

☀️ Annual team retreat


Want to learn more?

  • About us

  • Xelix blog

  • Xelix news

  • Xelix glassdoor

We believe that people from diverse backgrounds, with different identities and experiences make our company and product better. No matter your background, we'd love to hear from you! And if you have a disability, please let us know if there's any way we can make the interview process better for you - we're happy to accommodate!

If you're a recruiting agency - we have an existing list of agencies we work with if required and we are not currently planning on expanding the list. Neither the Talent team nor hiring managers or the Support team will respond to cold outreach.

This is a full-time position, with standard working hours from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday.

Interview Process
While the exact process may vary slightly depending on the role, our typical interview stages are:

  1. Introductory Call – A short Teams conversation with a Talent Partner to discuss your background and the opportunity.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview – A 30–45 minute Teams meeting to explore your experience and fit for the team.

  3. Technical Task or Presentation – A role-relevant exercise to demonstrate your skills and approach.

  4. Final On-site Interview – An in-person meeting with our senior leadership team and co-founders at our office.

We strive to make the process clear, efficient, and respectful of your time.

We welcome the responsible use of AI for research and interview preparation, but ask that it isn't used to generate answers during live interviews. We also believe in being transparent - we use Metaview's AI note-taker during interviews so our interviewers can stay fully present. If you'd prefer us not to use it, just let your interviewer know. While you may need to answer eligibility questions as part of your application, we do not use AI to review or make decisions on applications - every application is reviewed fairly by a member of our Talent team.

closest.title: Full Stack Developer Intern
closest.text:
Xendit provides payment infrastructure across Southeast Asia and is expanding to Greater China and LATAM. We process payments, power marketplaces, disburse payroll and loans, provide KYC solutions, prevent fraud, and help businesses grow exponentially. We serve our customers by providing a suite of world-class APIs, eCommerce platform integrations, and easy to use applications for individual entrepreneurs, SMEs, and enterprises alike.

Our main focus is building the most advanced payment rails for Southeast Asia, with a clear goal in mind — to make payments across and within SEA simple, secure and easy for everyone. We serve thousands of businesses ranging from SMEs to multinational enterprises, and process millions of transactions monthly. We’ve been growing rapidly since our inception in 2015, onboarding hundreds of new customers every month, and backed by global top-10 VCs. We’re proud to be featured on among the fastest growing companies by Y-Combinator.

About the Job

Duration: 6 months
Type: Internship

We’re looking for a Full Stack Developer Intern to help build and improve internal tools and web applications used by operational teams. You’ll work with engineers to ship real features across frontend, backend, APIs, data platforms, and deployment workflows.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or a related field.
  • Basic proficiency in JavaScript or TypeScript.
  • Familiarity with React and Node.js through coursework, personal projects, bootcamps, or previous experience.
  • Understanding of HTTP, REST APIs, Git, and relational or NoSQL databases.
  • Basic SQL knowledge.
  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar tools and asking good questions.
  • Able to communicate clearly in English and work collaboratively.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Next.js, Fastify, Express, or similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, CI/CD, or GitHub Actions/Buddy.
  • Familiarity with BigQuery, data pipelines, ETL/ELT, dbt, Airflow, or Databricks.
  • Exposure to Redis, PostgreSQL, message queues, or server-side background jobs.
  • Experience building projects deployed beyond localhost.
  • Interest in AI-assisted workflows, browser automation, or data platforms.

Tech you may work with

TypeScript, React, Vite/Next.js, Node.js, Fastify, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, BigQuery, SQL, ArgoCD, Terraform, and Git-based CI/CD.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain web interfaces using React and TypeScript.
  • Develop backend APIs and services using Node.js/TypeScript.
  • Integrate services with databases, REST APIs, queues, and third-party platforms.
  • Help build data integrations that read from or write to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and BigQuery.
  • Support data querying, validation, and operational reporting using SQL and BigQuery.
  • Write clean, tested, maintainable code and participate in code reviews.
  • Help debug issues across the application stack.
  • Assist with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and cloud deployment tasks.
  • Collaborate with product, operations, data, and engineering stakeholders to turn requirements into working features.
  • Document technical decisions and implementation details.

KOTLIN – WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE? March 12, 2026 Hire an app developer—this is often the very first step companies and entrepreneurs take when planning to launch a mobile application. With the demand for mobile app development growing year after year, choosing the right developer has become more critical than ever. The mobile app market is projected to surpass $600 billion by 2025, creating an environment filled with opportunities but also intense competition and varied pricing. Careful planning and selecting a skilled developer can make the difference between an app that stands out and one that gets lost in the crowd. Anyone looking for app developer services needs to carefully evaluate options that align with their budget, project requirements, and timeline. Choosing the right development model is key to ensuring success. This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to hire an app developer , covering hiring models, pricing structures, popular platforms, and effective selection strategies. With the right approach, you can find a developer who not only meets your technical needs but also helps turn your app idea into a market-ready product. Four Models for Hiring an App Developer Companies can hire an app developer in several ways. The right choice depends on project size, deadlines, and available budget. Each of these models offers specific strengths that make it better suited to particular situations. Freelance App Developers Freelance developers can be found on platforms such as Fiverr, Upwork, and Freelancer. They are cost-effective for smaller assignments but require close oversight. Communication issues and time zones can slow progress, so careful review of ratings and portfolios is important. In-House Development Team An in-house team works directly inside the company. This approach gives close supervision and quick discussions but requires a higher budget due to salaries, benefits, and office costs. It suits companies with ongoing, long-term development work. Hiring an App Development Company Development companies provide complete services, from design to testing, with an established team. This model costs more than freelance work but offers organized planning and reliable delivery, making it suitable for complex or time-sensitive projects. Staff Augmentation Staff augmentation adds a specialist to an existing team for a limited period. It works well when specific expertise is missing in-house. Once the specialized work is done, the engagement ends. Hourly Cost for Hiring Developers The cost of finding app developers depends on location, experience, and the type of agreement. Rates vary significantly between freelance developers and structured development companies. Reviewing these figures helps during early planning and provides a realistic picture of how budget expectations change by region. Freelance Developer Hourly Rates Freelancers usually work on a per‑project or hourly basis. Their rates depend on expertise and the complexity of the assigned tasks. The following table outlines the average hourly cost of freelance app development talent. Position United States Europe Asia Mid-Level Developer $132 $35 $24 Senior Developer $154 $45 $30 UI and UX Designer $79 $35 $25 Company Hourly Rates Companies charge hourly rates that include planning, design, coding, and testing with an established team. These services cost more than freelancers but offer broader support and structured oversight. The table below shows the typical range of hourly costs for mobile app development companies in different regions. Region iOS Development Android Development North America 150 to 200 168 to 250 Europe and UK 50 to 125 70 to 150 India and Pakistan 15 to 75 10 to 70 These comparisons provide a clear view of how much it might cost to hire freelance developers or an app development company, making it easier to plan budgets and choose the most practical location for your project. Where to Find App Developers Several paths can be used to find and hire a mobile app developer . Some approaches focus on online research, while others emphasize personal meetings or recommendations. Each method offers a different way to evaluate experience and reliability before making a decision. Online Platforms Online platforms provide an accessible starting point for finding developers. LinkedIn and Glassdoor are often used by companies that need full-time employees. Platforms such as Upwork and Toptal are popular choices when looking for freelance developers who have documented experience with projects. Business directories like Clutch and GoodFirms list professional app development companies and include ratings and client reviews that can guide selection. Industry Events Industry events are another effective method for finding development talent. Conferences such as Developer Week, GITEX, and the Gartner Summits bring together companies, developers, and project managers. Meeting in person at these events allows you to examine previous work, ask detailed questions, and build connections that may be useful when planning future projects. Referrals from Your Network Referrals are a trusted source when searching for developers. Colleagues, partners, or clients can introduce you to developers or companies that they have already worked with successfully. This reduces the time needed for screening because a recommended developer usually has a record of reliable work and proven results. Choosing the Right Hiring Model Selecting the correct hiring model depends on the priorities and limitations of your project. Timelines, the level of technical expertise required, and available financial resources will influence which option is the most practical. The following points explain three common situations and the type of finding app developers and the hiring arrangement that fits each case. Projects With Strict Delivery Dates If a project has strict delivery dates, a professional app development company is the most suitable choice. These companies have structured teams that coordinate schedules to meet fixed timelines. They also manage technical challenges internally so that unexpected issues do not delay the release. Projects That Need Specialized Knowledge When a project requires skills that your team does not have, staff augmentation becomes a practical option. This approach allows you to bring in a developer with specific expertise for a defined period. Once the specialized work is complete, the engagement ends and your team resumes control of the remaining tasks. Projects With a Limited Budget For projects that must be delivered with limited financial resources, outsourcing to regions such as Eastern Europe or South Asia can help manage costs. Teams in these regions often provide experienced developers at lower hourly rates. Freelancers can also be considered for smaller apps where the full support of a company is not needed. An overseas company provides a balanced option when cost control and skilled work are both priorities. Steps to Prepare Before Hiring Start with a detailed list of requirements for the application. Include the platform, the core features, and the technologies you prefer, such as Java, Kotlin, Swift, or Flutter. Use these details to evaluate developers who have experience with similar work. When possible, explore internal service links like hire a Python developer or hire Java developers to find specialists. Always request a portfolio to see previous work. Look for projects with similar complexity and functionality. Costs must be viewed as an investment and should be planned at the beginning of the process. Reviews and ratings on verified sites can provide an accurate picture of past performance. Before sharing project details, sign a non-disclosure agreement to protect your idea. Decide on a payment structure that is based on stages so that funds are released as progress is confirmed. Plan for app maintenance from the beginning because an app will need continuous updates after launch. Risks to Avoid During the Hiring Process Failing to sign an agreement can expose your app idea to others before the project begins. Paying the entire cost upfront without a payment schedule may also lead to risk if the quality does not meet your expectations. Always include maintenance services in the scope because an app needs continuous attention once it is live. Ignoring these points can affect your budget and may lead to incomplete work. Conclusion When the decision is made to hire an app developer , preparation and careful selection are essential. Each hiring model has its own benefits depending on the project’s needs. With clear planning, accurate cost assessments, and thorough portfolio reviews, you can confidently hire a mobile app developer who will deliver high-quality results while staying within budget and deadlines. Meeting in person at these events allows you to examine previous work, ask detailed questions, and build connections that may be useful when planning future projects. Referrals from Your Network Referrals are a trusted source when searching for developers. Colleagues, partners, or clients can introduce you to developers or companies that they have already worked with successfully. This reduces the time needed for screening because a recommended developer usually has a record of reliable work and proven results. Choosing the Right Hiring Model Selecting the correct hiring model depends on the priorities and limitations of your project. Timelines, the level of technical expertise required, and available financial resources will influence which option is the most practical. The following points explain three common situations and the type of finding app developers and the hiring arrangement that fits each case. Projects With Strict Delivery Dates If a project has strict delivery dates, a professional app development company is the most suitable choice. These companies have structured teams that coordinate schedules to meet fixed timelines. They also manage technical challenges internally so that unexpected issues do not delay the release. Projects That Need Specialized Knowledge When a project requires skills that your team does not have, staff augmentation becomes a practical option. This approach allows you to bring in a developer with specific expertise for a defined period. Once the specialized work is complete, the engagement ends and your team resumes control of the remaining tasks. Projects With a Limited Budget For projects that must be delivered with limited financial resources, outsourcing to regions such as Eastern Europe or South Asia can help manage costs. Teams in these regions often provide experienced developers at lower hourly rates. Freelancers can also be considered for smaller apps where the full support of a company is not needed. An overseas company provides a balanced option when cost control and skilled work are both priorities. Steps to Prepare Before Hiring Start with a detailed list of requirements for the application. Include the platform, the core features, and the technologies you prefer, such as Java, Kotlin, Swift, or Flutter. Use these details to evaluate developers who have experience with similar work. When possible, explore internal service links like hire a Python developer or hire Java developers to find specialists. Always request a portfolio to see previous work. Look for projects with similar complexity and functionality. Costs must be viewed as an investment and should be planned at the beginning of the process. Reviews and ratings on verified sites can provide an accurate picture of past performance. Before sharing project details, sign a non-disclosure agreement to protect your idea. Decide on a payment structure that is based on stages so that funds are released as progress is confirmed. Plan for app maintenance from the beginning because an app will need continuous updates after launch. Risks to Avoid During the Hiring Process Failing to sign an agreement can expose your app idea to others before the project begins. Paying the entire cost upfront without a payment schedule may also lead to risk if the quality does not meet your expectations. Always include maintenance services in the scope because an app needs continuous attention once it is live. Ignoring these points can affect your budget and may lead to incomplete work. Conclusion When the decision is made to hire an app developer , preparation and careful selection are essential. Each hiring model has its own benefits depending on the project’s needs. With clear planning, accurate cost assessments, and thorough portfolio reviews, you can confidently hire a mobile app developer who will deliver high-quality results while staying within budget and deadlines. closest.title: Mechanical Design Engineer
closest.text: Mechanical Design Engineer Mechanical Design Responsibilities: Create 2D and 3D designs for mechanical systems, emphasizing real-world functionality. Use advanced CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, AutoCAD) for precise design drawings. Optimize individual parts for performance. Develop prototypes to validate functionality, assembly, and performance. Conduct tolerance analyses to meet safety standards and evaluate prototypes. Participate in design reviews, provide technical guidance, and troubleshoot challenges. Knowledge of detail assembly drawing. Calculations in kinematics, dynamics, pneumatics, and servo motion analysis required for designing automation mechanisms and equipment. Mechanical Design Requirements: Proficiency in CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, AutoCAD, CATIA) and other relevant design and analysis tools. 3+ years in mechanical design for robotics or automation systems with a strong focus on real design, part, and component design. Strong understanding of robotics principles, kinematics, and control systems. Knowledge of industry standards and regulations relevant to mechanical engineering (e.g., ASME, ISO). In-depth knowledge of design for manufacturability and design for assembly principles. Experience with industrial or collaborative robots. Experience in rapid prototyping and 3D printing technologies is preferred. Familiarity with simulation and modelling tools, such as ROS (Robot Operating System) is preferred. Extensive experience in finite element analysis (FEA) and simulation, specifically focused on part and component behavior is preferred.

methodologies Strong attention to detail and ability to identify minor defects Critical thinking and problem-solving skills Excellent written and oral communication skills to convey technical API testing and integration Familiarity with performance testing tools like LoadRunner Experience with DevOps practices and tools Understanding of security testing and security best practices Engineer Do? A QA Engineer tests , validates , and debugs software products throughout the development lifecycle to ensure they meet quality standards and requirements before release. They intentionally identify and eliminate defects that could negatively impact user experience and customer satisfaction. Organizations need QA Engineers to protect customer trust and prevent costly post-release issues. QA Engineers help companies avoid technical debt by catching problems early in development, reducing the risk of security flaws, reputation damage, and expensive fixes after launch. Their work enables businesses to deliver reliable products that meet user expectations consistently. QA Engineers need strong technical skills including proficiency in programming languages like Java, Python, and JavaScript, along with expertise in manual and automated testing frameworks. They must possess excellent problem-solving abilities, critical thinking, attention to detail, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with developers and stakeholders throughout the testing process. What Are the Responsibilities of a QA Engineer? The responsibilities of a QA Engineer are to test software throughout development, identify defects, create automated testing solutions, and ensure products meet quality standards before release. QA Engineer duties include designing and implementing test cases, analyzing results, documenting findings, and collaborating with development teams to resolve issues. They verify software compatibility across multiple platforms and devices while maintaining comprehensive documentation of all testing procedures and outcomes. Understanding these core responsibilities helps organizations ask relevant interview questions about testing methodologies, automation experience, and problem-solving approaches, which are essential for identifying and hiring the best QA Engineer candidates who can deliver quality products consistently. Interview Questions By Amit Anand ■ May 19, 2026 ■ 11 min read These QA Engineer interview questions will guide your interview process to help you find trusted candidates with the right skills you are looking for. Contents 33 QA Engineer Interview Questions Technical Skills and Tools Testing Methodologies and Processes Problem-Solving and Defect Management Collaboration and Communication 33 QA Engineer Interview Questions What programming languages are you proficient in? What test automation tools and frameworks are you familiar with? Describe your experience with API testing and the tools you use How do you use browser DevTools in your testing process? What is your experience with SQL and database testing? Have you worked with CI/CD tools? Describe your experience What bug tracking and test management tools have you used? How do you approach cross-browser and cross-device testing? Explain the difference between manual and automated testing. When would you use each? Walk me through your process for creating test cases What types of testing are you experienced with? Describe your experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies How do you prioritize which tests to run when time is limited? What is regression testing and why is it important? Explain the software testing lifecycle you follow How do you perform exploratory testing? What is your experience with performance and load testing? How do you approach security testing? Describe a particularly challenging bug you found. How did you identify and report it? How do you write an effective bug report? How do you determine the severity and priority of a bug? Tell me about a time when developers disagreed with a bug you reported. How did you handle it? What do you do when you can't reproduce a reported bug? How do you handle situations where there's not enough time to test everything thoroughly? Describe your approach to root cause analysis when investigating defects How do you test features when requirements are unclear or incomplete? How do you collaborate with developers during the development process? Describe a time when you had to explain a technical issue to a non-technical stakeholder How do you ensure effective communication within your QA team? What role does QA play in sprint planning and retrospectives? How do you handle disagreements about whether something is a bug or a feature? Describe your experience working with product managers and understanding user requirements How do you communicate testing progress and quality metrics to leadership? Download QA Engineer Interview Questions PDF Technical Skills and Tools What programming languages are you proficient in? What to Listen For: Specific mention of relevant languages like Java, Python, C#, JavaScript, or SQL that align with your tech stack Concrete examples of how they've used these languages in testing scenarios, not just theoretical knowledge Awareness of which languages are best suited for different types of testing (e.g., Selenium with Java for UI automation) What test automation tools and frameworks are you familiar with? What to Listen For: Knowledge of industry-standard tools like Selenium, JUnit, Postman, TestRail, or Cypress that match your environment Practical experience implementing and maintaining automated test suites, not just familiarity with tool names Understanding of when to use automation versus manual testing and how to select appropriate tools Describe your experience with API testing and the tools you use What to Listen For: Hands-on experience with API testing tools like Postman, REST Assured, or SoapUI with specific examples Understanding of REST and SOAP protocols, HTTP methods, status codes, and API authentication mechanisms Ability to validate request/response structures, handle edge cases, and create comprehensive API test scenarios How do you use browser DevTools in your testing process? What to Listen For: Practical knowledge of Inspect, Console, and Network tabs to identify issues like JavaScript errors or failed requests Ability to debug frontend issues, analyze page performance, and understand client-server communication Experience using DevTools to support developers with detailed bug reports containing technical diagnostics What is your experience with SQL and database testing? What to Listen For: Ability to write basic to intermediate SQL queries to verify data integrity and validate backend operations Experience querying databases to confirm that UI actions correctly update underlying data Understanding of data validation strategies including checking for duplicates, null values, and referential integrity Have you worked with CI/CD tools? Describe your experience What to Listen For: Familiarity with CI/CD platforms like Jenkins, GitLab CI, CircleCI, or GitHub Actions Experience integrating automated tests into deployment pipelines to catch issues early Understanding of how automated testing fits into continuous delivery workflows and release processes What bug tracking and test management tools have you used? What to Listen For: Experience with tools like JIRA, Trello, TestRail, Zephyr, or similar platforms for tracking defects Ability to write clear, detailed bug reports with reproduction steps, screenshots, and severity classifications Understanding of defect lifecycle management and collaboration with development teams through these tools How do you approach cross-browser and cross-device testing? What to Listen For: Strategies for testing across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and identifying compatibility issues Experience with mobile testing on different devices, screen sizes, and operating systems (iOS, Android) Knowledge of testing tools like BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, or device farms for comprehensive coverage Testing Methodologies and Processes Explain the difference between manual and automated testing. When would you use each? What to Listen For: Clear understanding that manual testing involves human exploration while automation uses scripts for repetitive tests Recognition that manual testing is ideal for exploratory, usability, and ad-hoc scenarios while automation suits regression and repetitive tasks Balanced perspective acknowledging both methods have value and the best approach combines them strategically Walk me through your process for creating test cases What to Listen For: Systematic approach starting with understanding requirements and acceptance criteria before writing tests Inclusion of test case components like preconditions, test steps, expected results, and actual results Consideration of positive, negative, and edge case scenarios to ensure comprehensive coverage What types of testing are you experienced with? What to Listen For: Knowledge of various testing types including functional, regression, integration, performance, security, and UAT Specific examples demonstrating hands-on experience with multiple testing methodologies Understanding of when each testing type is appropriate in the software development lifecycle Describe your experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies What to Listen For: Familiarity with Agile ceremonies like sprint planning, daily standups, retrospectives, and sprint reviews Understanding of how QA fits into sprints, including early involvement in story refinement and continuous testing Experience collaborating closely with cross-functional teams and adapting to changing requirements How do you prioritize which tests to run when time is limited? What to Listen For: Risk-based testing approach focusing on critical functionality, high-traffic features, and areas with frequent defects Ability to balance business priorities with technical considerations when making testing decisions Communication with stakeholders about testing coverage and potential risks when shortcuts are necessary What is regression testing and why is it important? What to Listen For: Clear explanation that regression testing ensures existing features still work after code changes Recognition that it prevents new bugs from being introduced and catches unintended side effects Understanding of how automation makes regression testing more efficient and sustainable Explain the software testing lifecycle you follow What to Listen For: Knowledge of phases including requirement analysis, test planning, test case development, test execution, and closure Understanding of how testing integrates with the overall software development lifecycle (SDLC) Awareness of iterative testing approaches and continuous feedback loops in modern development How do you perform exploratory test

Contents Objectives Responsibilities Required Skills & Qualifications Preferred Skills & Qualifications What Does a QA Engineer Do? What Are the Responsibilities of a QA Engineer? Objectives Ensure software products meet quality standards and requirements before release Protect customer trust by identifying and eliminating defects that could negatively impact user experience Reduce long-term technical debt by catching issues early in the development lifecycle Support continuous delivery by maintaining rigorous testing standards that balance speed and quality Prevent costly post-release defects, security flaws, and reputation damage Enable product teams to scale releases with confidence while maintaining quality Improve overall product usability and customer satisfaction upon launch Responsibilities Test software products throughout the development lifecycle to identify bugs, glitches, and functionality issues Design and implement manual and automated test cases, test scripts, and testing programs Monitor and validate software at every stage of product development Analyze testing results and communicate findings to developers and stakeholders Document procedures, test results, bug reports, and quality metrics Verify software compatibility across devices, networks, operating systems, and platforms Create stable testing environments using continuous integration and testing automation Review and debug individual lines of code to catch small issues before they become major problems Collaborate with cross-functional teams including developers, designers, and product managers Participate in discovery, roadmap planning, feature prioritization, and OKR planning sessions Track quality issues and maintain comprehensive documentation throughout the project timeline Repeat and verify testing for previously identified issues to ensure proper resolution Identify areas for improvement in testing processes and methodologies Make suggestions during the product design phase to ensure testability Conduct final product reviews before commercial release to verify all quality requirements are met Required Skills & Qualifications Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information technology, or related field 2+ years of experience in software development, software testing, or quality assurance roles Proficiency in programming languages such as Java, JavaScript, Python, C#, or Ruby Expertise in software testing and A/B testing tools Strong knowledge of manual and automated testing processes and frameworks Experience with testing automation tools such as Selenium, QA Wolf, or Testim Ability to build and perform test analysis and verify quality requirements Experience with software debugging tools and integrated development environment (IDE) programs Knowledge of continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices Understanding of software development lifecycle and testing methodologies Strong attention to detail and ability to identify minor defects Critical thinking and problem-solving skills Excellent written and oral communication skills to convey technical information to both technical and non-technical stakeholders Ability to work collaboratively in team settings with developers, designers, and product managers Preferred Skills & Qualifications Master's degree or doctorate in computer science, engineering, or related field Certifications such as Certified Quality Assurance Professional (CQAP) Previous experience as a software developer or in software development roles Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Knowledge of Agile and Scrum methodologies Familiarity with project management tools like Jira Experience testing for desktop, mobile, console, and web platforms Understanding of database management systems including SQL and NoSQL Experience with version control systems such as Git and GitHub Knowledge of API testing and integration Familiarity with performance testing tools like LoadRunner Experience with DevOps practices and tools Understanding of security testing and security best practices Experience in specific industries such as automotive, healthcare, or finance Active participation in quality assurance communities and continuous learning through online courses What Does a QA Engineer Do? A QA Engineer tests , validates , and debugs software products throughout the development lifecycle to ensure they meet quality standards and requirements before release. They intentionally identify and eliminate defects that could negatively impact user experience and customer satisfaction. Organizations need QA Engineers to protect customer trust and prevent costly post-release issues. QA Engineers help companies avoid technical debt by catching problems early in development, reducing the risk of security flaws, reputation damage, and expensive fixes after launch. Their work enables businesses to deliver reliable products that meet user expectations consistently. QA Engineers need strong technical skills including proficiency in programming languages like Java, Python, and JavaScript, along with expertise in manual and automated testing frameworks. They must possess excellent problem-solving abilities, critical thinking, attention to detail, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with developers and stakeholders throughout the testing process. What Are the Responsibilities of a QA Engineer? The responsibilities of a QA Engineer are to test software throughout development, identify defects, create automated testing solutions, and ensure products meet quality standards before release. QA Engineer duties include designing and implementing test cases, analyzing results, documenting findings, and collaborating with development teams to resolve issues. They verify software compatibility across multiple platforms and devices while maintaining comprehensive documentation of all testing procedures and outcomes. Understanding these core responsibilities helps organizations ask relevant interview questions about testing methodologies, automation experience, and problem-solving approaches, which are essential for identifying and hiring the best QA Engineer candidates who can deliver quality products consistently. closest.title: Manufacturing Engineer Technician
closest.text: Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth. With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection. As an Manufacturing Engineer Technician focused on wire harnessing, you will be the hands-on bridge between engineering design and flight-ready hardware. You will be directly responsible for building, integrating, and testing the complex electrical arteries of our spacecraft and payload systems. We operate in a dynamic, prototype-to-production environment where you will not just follow instructions, but actively work to improve them. We want individuals with a deep sense of ownership who are relentless about quality and thrive in manufacturing environments. What You Will Do - First-Article Harnessing: Build, route, and test prototype and first-article wire harnesses, documenting the best methods for mass production. - Process Development: Work with manufacturing engineers to draft, redline, and finalize work instructions and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the factory floor. - Production Setup: Assist in the physical layout and organization of our newly renovated production rooms and R&D labs, helping to establish efficient feeder cells and the main satellite pulse line. - System Integration: Cleanly integrate harnesses and avionics onto the spacecraft, directly interfacing with GNC and mechanical systems. - Digital Tracking: Utilize our MES to log build progress, track material flow, and report defects, providing feedback to the engineering team on how to make the workflow smoother. - Tooling & Equipment: Help design, assemble, and maintain custom manufacturing jigs, fixtures, and harnessing boards. - Quality & Verification: Perform electrical continuity testing and quality checks, ensuring all hardware meets strict aerospace-grade standards before moving down the line. What We Are Looking For - High school diploma or equivalency certificate. - 1 to 3 years of hands-on experience in a manufacturing technician, harnessing, or prototype assembly role within aerospace, eVTOL, advanced automotive, or robotics. - Strong practical knowledge of wire harnessing (cutting, stripping, crimping, soldering) and the associated mechanical/electronic hand tools. - Proven ability to read and interpret technical schematics, wiring diagrams, and mechanical blueprints. - A process oriented mindset with a track record of identifying inefficiencies and suggesting practical improvements on the shop floor. - Willingness to work onsite full-time in Burlingame, CA. Bonus Points - Experience transitioning hardware from an R&D lab environment into a structured production line. - Hands-on experience working inside cleanrooms and managing Foreign Object Debris (FOD). - Familiarity with 5S principles and lean manufacturing concepts. For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC). For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Bonus Points - Experience transitioning hardware from an R&D lab environment into a structured production line. - Hands-on experience working inside cleanrooms and managing Foreign Object Debris (FOD). - Familiarity with 5S principles and lean manufacturing concepts. For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC). For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

closest.title: Computer Vision Engineer
closest.text: Do you get excited about building cutting-edge perception systems that work reliably in the real world? Do you have a strong foundation in computer vision, robotics, or sensor fusion? Are you interested in shaping new technology capabilities within a growing and innovative high-tech company, where people and fun are part of our core values? We’d love to have you! Who is Xsens Xsens is a leading full-stack provider of sensors, software, and analytics that enable the digitization of movement. Xsens serves entertainment, humanoid robotics, health & sports and automation & mobility markets. By turning complex motion data into actionable insight, we help our partners accelerate development, improve control and learning, and bring physically intelligent systems to life. We collaborate with leading global innovators including Boston Dynamics, Toyota, Siemens, Electronic Arts, Epic Games, Netflix, and 20th Century Studios, alongside more than 1,000 research institutions, humanoid robotics companies and universities worldwide. Your role as a Computer Vision Engineer at Xsens As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will be at the heart of our effort to expand Xsens' positioning and localization capabilities, moving beyond inertial-only solutions toward full visual-inertial systems. You will research, prototype, and deploy algorithms for Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), SLAM, and 6-DoF pose estimation, bringing together our IMU technologies with camera-based perception capabilities. You will be part of the Technology team and report to the Technology Manager. You will be based in Enschede, the Netherlands, with the possibility of hybrid working. We actively leverage Generative AI tools to accelerate development and improve quality. You are expected to embrace these tools as part of your workflow and continuously explore how they can enhance development, experimentation, and performance. Key responsibilities: Design and implement state-of-the-art VIO and SLAM pipelines, combining inertial sensor data with monocular or stereo camera inputs. Develop and maintain camera models, calibration routines, and sensor synchronization pipelines across multiple hardware configurations. Apply optimization techniques and filtering methods to achieve robust and accurate 6-DoF pose estimation. Stay current with the computer vision and research landscape and assess the feasibility of integrating new techniques into Xsens products. Collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and software teams to deliver end-to-end perception solutions. Xsens is looking for a hands-on Computer Vision Engineer who combines strong theoretical foundations with a proven ability to build and ship working systems. Required MSc in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, with 3+ years of relevant industry or research experience; or a PhD with demonstrated hands-on system-building experience Solid understanding of multi-view geometry and camera and lens models and physics Hands-on experience with VO or SLAM systems, and familiarity with open source frameworks Proficiency in Python / C++ Strong mathematical background in linear algebra, probability theory, and state estimation. Preferred A few years of experience in automotive and/or robotics industry Experience with IMU signal processing and inertial sensor models Awareness of GPU-accelerated computing and experience in optimizing algorithms for real-time performance Knowledge of deep learning-based perception methods Experience with ROS, OpenCV, and standard robotics tooling. Working at Xsens We value ingenious ideas, no matter where they come from. We believe diverse thoughts, voices, and backgrounds make us stronger as a company. We know that it is through collaboration with people from all walks of life that we make the most positive impact as an organization. Join Xsens’ innovative, ambitious, and international team, where your ideas and talents make an impact. Along with a competitive compensation package, we offer a range of benefits designed to support your well-being and help you thrive. 28 paid vacation days with an option to buy, sell, or carry over days, giving you flexibility to manage your time off as appropriate to your situation Tax perks for your sports memberships and bicycle purchase; so staying active is easier than ever. Flexible working hours and the option to work from home, helping you balance life and work Paid volunteer time: Through our partnership with Stichting Present, you have the opportunity to give back to the community during office hours Our partnership with Equip gives you on-demand access to a dedicated financial planner who provides clear guidance and a concrete plan for wealth building, pensions, and major life events. Enjoy company social events as well as fun, informal activities organized by our staff association. From movie nights and sports clinics to cooking classes and LAN parties, there’s always something happening to connect and have fun

closest.text:
About XP Health

At XP Health, we're on a mission to revolutionize vision care through cutting-edge technology, including augmented reality, while ensuring a delightful and seamless user experience. We aim to make high-quality eye care accessible to everyone. Today, we are honored to serve over 3,000 clients, including several Fortune 500 logos and notable Silicon Valley companies. With passionate founders and a team that boasts deep expertise in the field, XP Health has driven efficient, best-in-class growth to date, and is hungry for more. 

We invite you to become part of our dynamic and diverse team, where unique perspectives meet unparalleled growth opportunities. With over $50M in funding raised, including our Series B round in early 2024, we’re positioned for exciting new challenges and impactful contributions to the healthcare landscape.

Your impact and responsibilities

  • Transform visiting the eye doctor into an enjoyable and delightful experience for a BILLION people
  • Tackle challenges to provide responsive and engaging customer experiences while ensuring user data is being handled securely and with care
  • Design, implement, and test brand new product features having top-line business impact and performance (delightful customer facing features and internal tools improving productivity)
  • Build tools to deploy, monitor, and manage our applications
  • Conduct code reviews and provide regular feedback to your team
  • Keep up to date with the latest web technologies and infrastructure designs

What we’re looking for

  • BS/MS in CS, related technical field, or equivalent industry experience
  • 5+ years of object oriented programming experience in a professional environment
  • Experience building secure, production-level, backend infrastructure
  • Experience working with AWS services (e.g. S3, ElasticBeanstalk, EC2)
  • Experience in web technologies such as ES6, React, Node, Redux, jQuery, Webpack, Babel, SCSS
  • Passion for creating great user experiences
  • Ability to work in a cross functional environment (non-engineers such as designers, doctors, and end customers)
  • Self-starter, adaptable, coachable, and excited to work in a fast-moving startup environment
  • Our team is Hybrid in our San Carlos Office

Nice to haves

  • Former founder or early engineer at a startup
  • Mobile development experience
  • Experience working with Augmented Reality

Why join us?

  • Passionate founders with pedigree relevant to the space (Forbes 30 under 30, ex-Facebook and Airbnb, former board members and advisors at various companies)
  • Proven team with senior leadership and subject-matter expertise
  • Enormous market ($40B is spent annually in the US vision care, over $17B is going to waste annually)
  • Proven product market fit with over 20 corporate clients (and quickly expanding!)

Our Hiring Process:

We believe great engineering teams are built through thoughtful conversations, collaborative problem-solving, and a mutual understanding of how we work. Our interview process is designed to give you a clear view into our engineering culture while allowing us to understand your technical strengths and approach.

  • Stage 1 — Recruiter Screen

Best hardware to become an AR or VR developer December 23, 2021 - By Casey Armstrong Kudos to you! It’s exciting to see that you are considering becoming an AR or VR developer. We look forward to helping you navigate the world of XR development and design, starting with hardware advice… Side note: You might notice that this is a long article, but do not fear! We are here to help. We wrote this as a guide to help potential students learn about their hardware situation, but we are also here to talk with you if you get stuck. At any point, you can reach out to support@xrterra.com , and we can advise you on your hardware buying decisions. So, you want to learn to develop for VR or AR … One of the first steps in your journey, will be figuring out if you need to buy anything in order to get started. We’re guessing you have a few questions, such as: Is my computer powerful enough for VR development? How do I connect my VR headset to my computer for development? (Do I actually need the Oculus link cable or will a 3rd party cable work?) Does my phone support Augmented Reality development? (Do iPhones work for augmented reality development?) And, we are eager to answer these questions, but before we do, we first want to make sure that we don’t waste any of your time! Not looking for a lesson in XR hardware right now? Rather, do you just want the best recommendation and to go ahead with it? If so, then here it is, here’s the hardware you need to become an AR or VR developer at XR Terra: Computer: An Oculus Link ready PC Windows 10 or higher 30 GB+ of free memory on an SSD hard drive Example: The Acer Predator 300 Gaming Laptop VR : A Quest 2 AR : An ARCore Compatible Android phone Example: The Google Pixel Hardware Compatibility The first thing to consider is device compatibility. Does your XR device match with your computer hardware? Check out this chart to see where you fall: Type of phone In addition to the information above, remember that your phone must also be able to work with ARCore https://developers.google.com/ar/discover/supported-devices Or ARKit if developing for the iPhone Now that we have our bases covered, let’s jump into it! Hardware requirements for developing XR applications with Unity boils down to 3 Things: Your Laptop or Desktop Computer An SSD Hard Drive (with lots of Free Memory) Your XR Device / Its Peripherals 1. Your Desktop or Laptop Before you make the decision to make any large purchases, keep in mind that most PC and Mac computers will be compatible with the software used in this course. To check if your machine is compatible, navigate to the Unity System Requirements document for Unity 2020 LTS and select ‘desktop’ to reach the minimum required hardware. In addition to the specs listed by Unity, your machine must fulfill these other basic requirements: Storage Requirements : 30GB SSD onboard ( not cloud storage ) USB : Port Minimum 1 x USB 3.0 or 1 x USB C ( Based on Mobile Device / VR Headset ) Any Webcam Mouse Middle Scroll Wheel ( needed for Unity navigation ) However, that is certainly not the end of the story… Since you’re reading this, you’re probably planning to go all-in on XR development, so we have a much better list of computer specs to aim for: Graphics Card: NVIDIA GTX 970 or greater CPU: Intel Core i5 (sixth generation or newer) or equivalent Memory: 8GB RAM or more Storage: 256GB SSD or more Video Output: DisplayPort 1.2 / Mini DisplayPort, HDMI USB Port: Minimum 1x USB 3.0 port, 1x USB C Connectivity: 802.11ac 2.4/5 GHz wireless adapter Operating System: Windows 10 preferred Other: Webcam Recommended Budget Option for using Oculus Link (which will allow you to playtest in Unity as well, making you a faster VR developer): Acer often sells the “Acer Predator 300” refurbished/recertified through their website or on Amazon. Keep in mind that this laptop is sold with different specifications in different places. So, we recommend that you double-check that the laptop you are buying, whatever the name listed, has at least the above specifications listed in its product description. 2. Is there Space on Your Hard Drive? You will want lots of space on your hard drive for XR development. Unity, 3D Models, design programs like Blender and Illustrator, and Visual Studio (and XCode if you have a Mac) will all fill-up your computer’s memory pretty fast! So, make sure you have at leaset 30 GB or more of onboard memory. Also, you will want an SSD (solid state hard drive) over a HDD (hard disk drive) because it is much faster. Speed will be very helpful when developing because you will be working with large files and large programs as part of your regular XR related workflow. 3. How do I pick the right VR device & AR device? VR: While we suggest keeping it simple by purchasing the Quest 2 , we can help you work with other headsets/platforms such as Vive , Valve , or Windows Mixed Reality , Pimax , etc. However, keep in mind that most of our lectures and supporting materials are targeting development for the Quest platform. AR: While we suggest keeping it simple by purchasing an older/refurbished phone (from Amazon or other online retailer), such as the Pixel 3 to name a good example, any ARCore or ARKit compatible phones will work. We will help you navigate building for other platforms such as the Hololens, etc., but that may have to be outside of the everyday lectures and may be more one-on-one and involve more troubleshooting, etc. Conclusion: Hopefully, this guide and the FAQ’s below will help you to get better acquainted with your hardware and help you understand your hardware needs to become an AR or VR developer. We know you can make the right decision! Nevertheless, buying a laptop or desktop, phone, and XR equipment is a big deal! It requires some thought. So, we are here to help if you get stuck. Please contact support@xrterra.com with any questions. We are happy to help! Hardware FAQ I have an older computer. Can I still use it as a VR developer?? Possibly! See the suggested specs listed earlier in the article. And, read here for the minimum requirements for Unity . Please reach out if you are still unsure. Do Mac computers work for XR development? Yes, but building for XR with Unity is much easier on a Windows PC. First, determine if your Mac is powerful enough to meet the minimum specs suggested earlier in this article. Second, see the hardware compatibility guide at the top of this article to see if you are ok with some of the limitations it may present. If you are confused about whether or not to use your Mac in the course, then please reach out to support@xrterra.com. Why is it harder to develop for VR with a Mac? If your VR headset is a standalone (running an Android OS), you can build and deploy an .apk file and upload to the headset via a USB C cable. This method, called ‘side-loading’, will take longer, slow you down, and feel less intuitive. Put another way, on Mac’s, you cannot playtest using Unity (directly to the headset) like you can on an Oculus Ready Windows PC. Playtesting is a method of quality control that takes place at many points of your development and design process. As you build VR apps, you will want to quickly check what your changes to the code are doing to your application. Without Oculus Link (which Mac cannot have/run), you will simply have to wait longer for the game to compile each and every time you want to see what your changes did to the VR app, etc. Should I get a desktop or a laptop for XR development? Both options are good, but laptops have a slight edge simply because manufacturers know that laptops sell well. So, laptops offer more competitive pricing, and they perform just as well in most cases. It’s also hard to beat the portability of a laptop vs. a desktop computer. Note: Laptop fans might be louder than desktop computer fans. How can I be budget conscious when shopping for a new laptop or desktop? Shop around. Ever since the pandemic started and it’s associated supply chain issues, it has made computers and computer parts more expensive, and price fluctuations can be unpredictable. The only way to combat this is to spend more time shopping and to be more patient, etc. Explore options from multiple online retailers, and search both refurbished and new options. Why do you recommend the Quest 2 for new VR developers? You can use any VR headset you want, but we’ve focused on the Quest 2 because it’s the most popular, the most affordable, and has the added benefit of running stand-alone, or tethered to a PC. The dual nature of stand alone and tethered (i.e., Oculus Link) allows you to use the Oculus Store as well as the Steam store for a much larger library of apps and games. Do I need a Facebook account to use the Quest? Currently, yes. However, Facebook accounts will not be required soon. Meta/Facebook will not require a Facebook account starting sometime in 2022. You can read more about this in this article . What AR compatible phones do you recommend? Budget: Pixel 2 or 3… Daily Driver: A Pixel 5 or higher. If you want a big screen or a Tablet Note 10 or higher in the Galaxy Note series Tablets that support AR Core Longevity: The more modern the phone, and the higher the quality, the longer it will last and receive software support and security updates. Development Phone: If you want to save money, and you consider this a phone only for development, the Samsung Galaxy S8 or 9 is a popular option that devs often use to do mobile development because it is such a popular android phone. What is Oculus Link? Is it required? Does it require a special cord? More information on Oculus link can be found here . Oculus Link is a software program that enables you to turn your Quest VR device into a PC VR experience by tethering your Quest to your PC. Oculus Link works via a high quality USB C cable or an official Oculus Link cord. It is not required. Instead of Oculus Link, you can use any USB C cable is needed to side-load .apk files to the headset. A high quality USB C or Oculus Link cable is needed for tethering to a PC, although now you can wirelessly connect your Quest to a PC (provided you have a fast Wifi-5 or preferably a Wifi-6 connection). What’s the difference between using Oculus Link for gaming and using Oculus Link for developing with Unity? They’re the same, using the Oculus Desktop (Windows) software. The software outputs the graphics through the cable to the headset (like a second monitor). For gaming, you’ll be playing PC VR titles, all processing is handled on the PC’s GPU and output through the link cable to the headset. For developing in Unity, you’ll be able to playtest your app directly to your headset (if you’re on a PC). Without Oculus Link, you cannot playtest using Unity directly to the headset. Playtesting is a method of quality control that takes place at many points of your development and design process. As you build VR apps, you will want to quickly check what your changes to the code are doing to your application. Without Oculus Link (which Mac cannot have/run), you will simply have to wait longer for the game to compile each and every time you want to see what your changes did to the VR app, etc. Check out this video demonstrating what playtesting in Unity looks like with Oculus Link. Does Oculus Link work on Mac? No (unless your Mac has Bootcamp and also has Windows installed). However, we do not recommend trying this. There are no guarantees that that would solve all issues,etc. If you want to use Oculus Link, we recommend sticking with a PC. What software can I use to test my computer to see specs, etc.? The Steam VR Performance test is a easy to use and free option for seeing if your computer is VR ready Here it is in action if you are curious what it looks like. Does what type of development I want to do affect what kind of hardware I should buy? Yes, VR and AR each require specific hardware. Please see the above descriptions for more information. What’s the best graphics card for VR? For good VR performance, Nvidia GTX 1060 or higher or check this chart to see about AMD GPU’s This is less of an issue if you do not plan to use Oculus Link or PC VR What’s the best CPU for VR development? i7 or Ryzen 7 are recommended However, i5 and Ryzen 5 (or lower) will be acceptable (without Oculus Link) for Windows, and any CPU for Mac will also be fine For a recent article on the best CPU for VR in 2021, check out this article . What about RAM? 8GB is workable However, we recommend 12 or 16GB of RAM if possible. How should I think about cost when budgeting for my VR hardware? Computers are a big investment, so plan accordingly. If you plan to develop for XR, then a more modern device and computer will save you a lot of time and guesswork, etc. However, keep in mind, if XR is just a hobby for you (or so

Playtesting is a method of quality control that takes place at many points of your development and design process. As you build VR apps, you will want to quickly check what your changes to the code are doing to your application. Without Oculus Link (which Mac cannot have/run), you will simply have to wait longer for the game to compile each and every time you want to see what your changes did to the VR app, etc. Check out this video demonstrating what playtesting in Unity looks like with Oculus Link. Does Oculus Link work on Mac? No (unless your Mac has Bootcamp and also has Windows installed). However, we do not recommend trying this. There are no guarantees that that would solve all issues,etc. If you want to use Oculus Link, we recommend sticking with a PC. What software can I use to test my computer to see specs, etc.? The Steam VR Performance test is a easy to use and free option for seeing if your computer is VR ready Here it is in action if you are curious what it looks like. Does what type of development I want to do affect what kind of hardware I should buy? Yes, VR and AR each require specific hardware. Please see the above descriptions for more information. What’s the best graphics card for VR? For good VR performance, Nvidia GTX 1060 or higher or check this chart to see about AMD GPU’s This is less of an issue if you do not plan to use Oculus Link or PC VR What’s the best CPU for VR development? i7 or Ryzen 7 are recommended However, i5 and Ryzen 5 (or lower) will be acceptable (without Oculus Link) for Windows, and any CPU for Mac will also be fine For a recent article on the best CPU for VR in 2021, check out this article . What about RAM? 8GB is workable However, we recommend 12 or 16GB of RAM if possible. How should I think about cost when budgeting for my VR hardware? Computers are a big investment, so plan accordingly.
